saa-med-097.text: Auditing the costs of S3, the team discovered relevant storage charges without corresponding visible objects: they are parts of multipart uploads that failed in the past and were never completed or aborted.?
options: Disable multipart uploads in pocket
Enable versioning to hide parts
Empty and recreate the pocket periodically
Create a life cycle rule that automatically aborts incomplete multipart uploads after N days
saa-med-097.explanation: The AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule removes the pending orphan parts and prevents future buildup — good practice recommended for any bucket receiving multipart uploads.
saa-med-097.hint: The failed uploads 'cracks' remain in the account — program the automatic life cycle broom.
optionRationales: The AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule removes the pending orphan parts and prevents future buildup — good practice recommended for any bucket receiving multipart uploads.
Re-create newsletters destroys valid data and processes — disproportionate to a problem that a rule solves.
Multipart is essential for reliable large uploads — the problem is not the resource, it is the lack of cleaning of incomplete.
Versioning does not interact with incomplete parts — and 'hidden' does not eliminate collection.

saa-med-098.text: A course platform has unpredictable and rare registration peaks (launchings), with low traffic in the rest of the time. The current architecture maintains a fixed fleet dimensioned to the peak. API for Lambda + API Gateway, which cost analysis is correct?
options: The serverless tends to cost less in this profile, because the cost accompanies the real requests and zeros idleness — while the fixed fleet pays the peak 24/7
Serverless is unfeasible because it can't handle registration peaks
Costs are identical in any traffic pattern
The fixed fleet is always cheaper because the Lambda collects per millisecond
saa-med-098.explanation: Loads with rare peaks and long valleys are the best case of the serverless: the dimensioned fleet for the peak wastes most of the time, and the Lambda charges only effective use, automatically climbing in launches.
saa-med-098.hint: Fixed fleet pays the show ticket every day; serverless only pays when the show happens.
optionRationales: Loads with rare peaks and long valleys are the best case of the serverless: the dimensioned fleet for the peak wastes most of the time, and the Lambda charges only effective use, automatically climbing in launches.
Covering per millisecond is just what zeros the cost in the valleys — in low use, the total serverless is far below the permanent fleet.
Models differ strongly according to use — high idleness favors serverless; constant intense use can favor instances with compromises.
The Lambda automatically scale to thousands of competing executions — sudden peaks are one of your strengths.

saa-med-099.text: An organization needs to group and miss costs of AWS according to business dimensions that do not exist in the tags (e.g. group dozens of accounts and tags in 'Unit Varejo' and 'Unit Attacked', with rules of error). AWS creates these custom dimensions in the reports?
options: Rename the member accounts with the unit name
AWS Cost Categories, defining rules that map accounts, tags and services in business categories
Export the invoice and sort it manually into spreadsheets
Create a separate organization for each business unit
saa-med-099.explanation: Cost Categories creates custom logical groupings (with rules on accounts, tags, services and even shared cost sharing) that appear in Cost Explorer, Budgets and CUR — the business vision layer on billing.
saa-med-099.hint: Above the tags there is a layer of 'categories' that translates the invoice to the business organogram.
optionRationales: Cost Categories creates custom logical groupings (with rules on accounts, tags, services and even shared cost sharing) that appear in Cost Explorer, Budgets and CUR — the business vision layer on billing.
Account names help visual identification, but do not create aggregate dimensions with rules of error in reports.
Fragmenting organisations breaks consolidated billing and governance — unnecessary when categories resolve in the reporting layer.
Recurring manual classification is laborious and prone to error — the native resource consistently automates this.

saa-med-100.text: After consolidating reports, FinOps team wants a prioritized and automatic list of account savings opportunities: instances that have been standing for weeks, orphaned volumes, oversized resources and commitments (Savings Plans) recommended based on use. AWS delivers these consolidated optimization recommendations?
options: AWS Cost Optimization Hub, which centralizes and prioritizes the recommendations of economy (right-sizing, idle resources, commitments) in one place
AWS CloudFormation Drift Detection
Amazon CloudWatch Services
AWS Resource Explorer
saa-med-100.explanation: Cost Optimization Hub adds recommendations from various sources (Compute Optimizer, Trusted Advisor, recommendations of the Savings Plans/RIs) with an estimate of economy, deduplication and prioritisation — the single window of opportunity.
saa-med-100.hint: Think of the hub that brings together all the economic tips spread by the services in a prioritized row.
optionRationales: Cost Optimization Hub adds recommendations from various sources (Compute Optimizer, Trusted Advisor, recommendations of the Savings Plans/RIs) with an estimate of economy, deduplication and prioritisation — the single window of opportunity.
Drift detection compares resources with the declared template — configuration governance, not cost optimization.
ServiceLens correlates traces and metrics of observability applications — no financial recommendations.
Resource Explorer seeks and invents resources between regions — does not estimate savings or prioritize opportunities.

saa-med-101.text: A company migrated its web application to EC2, but all instances and the Application Load Balancer (ALB) are configured in a single Availability Zone (AZ). The architecture team wants that, if this AZ becomes unavailable, the application continues to automatically meet users without manual intervention. Which architecture change meets this requirement in the simplest and most correct way.?
options: Configure the Auto Scaling Group to use subnets in at least two AZs and associate the ALB subnets in these same AZs.
Enable Multi-AZ only in the database RDS used by the application.
Increase the size (type) of the instances EC2 to support more load in case of peak.
Replace multiple instances with a single instance EC2 larger with an associated Elastic IP.
saa-med-101.explanation: Correct. Auto Scaling Group in multiple AZs sub-networks, EC2 Auto Scaling distributes the instances between them; if an AZ fails, the instances of this AZ are replaced in a healthy AZ, and the ALB (also with multiple AZs sub-networks) continues to route traffic to the entire destinations, without any manual intervention.
saa-med-101.hint: Think about how to distribute both the balancer and the Auto Scaling Group by multiple sub-networks in different AZs.
optionRationales: Correct. Auto Scaling Group in multiple AZs sub-networks, EC2 Auto Scaling distributes the instances between them; if an AZ fails, the instances of this AZ are replaced in a healthy AZ, and the ALB (also with multiple AZs sub-networks) continues to route traffic to the entire destinations, without any manual intervention.

Incorrect. Increasing the type of instance (vertical scaling) improves the processing capacity, but does not solve the problem of an entire AZ becoming unavailable — if all instances continue in a single AZ, the failure of this AZ would still bring down the entire application.

Incorrect. A single instance (even larger, with Elastic IP) is a single point of failure: if the instance or AZ where it resides fails, the application is totally unavailable until a manual recovery — the opposite of the automatic continuity goal.
Incorrect as a complete solution. RDS Multi-AZ protects the database layer, but does not resolve the unavailability of CAMADA WEB (cases EC2 and ALB), which is the focus of the scenario described.

saa-med-102.text: A database Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL hosts critical financial data. The operations team requires that, in case of failure of the primary database instance (e.g. hardware or AZ failure), automatic failover occurs for a replica in another AZ in a few minutes, SEM the application needs to change the connection endpoint. Which configuration meets this requirement?
options: Configure frequent database manual snapshots and restore them to another AZ if the primary instance fails.
Implant Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the database instance, without enabling Multi-AZ.
Create a Read Replica in another AZ and, in case of failure of the primary instance, manually promote it to the independent instance.
Enable Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for this database instance.
saa-med-102.explanation: Correct. RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronised standby instance in another AZ. In case of failure of the primary instance, the RDS performs automatic failover for standby and updates the log DNS of the endpoint to point to it — the application continues to use the same endpoint, without the need for manual reconfiguration, and the failure occurs typically in 1-2 minutes.
saa-med-102.hint: Think about the resource of RDS which maintains a standby instance synchronized into another AZ and performs automatic failure while preserving the same endpoint DNS.
optionRationales: Correct. RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronised standby instance in another AZ. In case of failure of the primary instance, the RDS performs automatic failover for standby and updates the log DNS of the endpoint to point to it — the application continues to use the same endpoint, without the need for manual reconfiguration, and the failure occurs typically in 1-2 minutes.

Incorrect. Read Replicas are designed for ESCALAR LEITURAS, use asynchronous replication and require PROMOTION MANUAL to become independent — moreover, when promoted, they receive a NOVO endpoint, requiring reconfiguration of the application. This does not meet the requirement of automatic failover with the same endpoint.

Incorrect. Restoring a snapshot creates a NOVA instance (with new endpoint) and may take a long time, besides not being automatic — this process does not meet the requirement to fail in a few minutes without manual intervention.

Incorrectly isolated. RDS Proxy Helps REDUZIR the connection time of the application during a failure (maintaining the connection pool), but it does not create or maintain the standby in another AZ — without the Multi-AZ enabled, there is no standby instance for which the failure can occur.

saa-med-103.text: A company owns a fleet of 5 cases EC2 Linux distributed in 2 Availability Zones. These instances need to share, in real time, a set of configuration files and user uploads — all instances must be able to LER and ESCREVER in the same files simultaneously, through a file system compatible with POSIX, remaining available even if one of the AZs fails. Which storage solution meets this requirement?
options: Create a file system Amazon EFS with mounting points (mount targets) in each of the AZs used and mount it in all instances.
Provide a file system Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and mount it in instances EC2 Linux.
Create a volume Amazon EBS and attach it to the 5 instances for everyone to read and write in the same files.
Store files in a pocket Amazon S3 and mount it in instances using a tool like s3fs.
saa-med-103.explanation: Correct. Amazon EFS is an elastic file system compatible with NFS/POSIX which can be mounted SIMULTANEAMENTE by multiple instances EC2, in multiple AZs, with concurrent reading and writing. By creating mount targets in each AZ, the EFS remains accessible even if an AZ is unavailable, taking into account both sharing and multi-AZ resilience.
saa-med-103.hint: Think about which storage service offers a file system POSIX elastic, assembled simultaneously by multiple instances in several AZs.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon EFS is an elastic file system compatible with NFS/POSIX which can be mounted SIMULTANEAMENTE by multiple instances EC2, in multiple AZs, with concurrent reading and writing. By creating mount targets in each AZ, the EFS remains accessible even if an AZ is unavailable, taking into account both sharing and multi-AZ resilience.

Incorrect. A volume EBS is linked to UMA ONLY AZ and even with the appeal EBS Multi-Attach, can only be attached to instances DENTRO DA MESMA AZ and requires a cluster recognition file system — does not meet the requirement of shared access between instances in different AZs.

Incorrect. S3 is a storage of OBJETOS, not a file system POSIX native; solutions such as s3fs are unofficial, have performance and inconsistent consistency semantics for files shared with frequent concurrent writings, unlike EFS, which was designed specifically for this use case.

Incorrect. FSx for Windows File Server is designed for Windows workloads using the protocol SMB and integration with Active Directory; Linux instances would require a file system compatible with NFS/POSIX, which is what Amazon EFS provides natively.

saa-med-104.text: An e-commerce team stores the product catalog images in a pocket Amazon S3. Recently, a script with bug SOBRESCREVEU several important images with corrupted versions. The team wants a form of RECUPERAR the previous versions of the affected objects, preventing permanent loss of data in similar future incidents (overwritten or accidental exclusions).?
options: Configure a Lifecycle Policy to move objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.
Configure Cross-Region Replication for a Bucket in another region.
Enable Versioning in the Bucket S3.
Create a routine that manually copies all the items from the bucket to another backup bucket once a week.
saa-med-104.explanation: Correct. With Version enabled, whenever an object is overwritten or deleted, the S3 preserves the previous version instead of discarding it (an exclusion only adds a 'delete marker'). This allows you to recover any previous version of an object, protecting against overwritten and accidental exclusions — exactly the scenario requirement.
saa-med-104.hint: Think about which configuration of the S3 automatically keeps copies of previous versions of an object whenever it is overwritten or deleted.
optionRationales: Correct. With Version enabled, whenever an object is overwritten or deleted, the S3 preserves the previous version instead of discarding it (an exclusion only adds a 'delete marker'). This allows you to recover any previous version of an object, protecting against overwritten and accidental exclusions — exactly the scenario requirement.

Incorrect as the main solution. CRR replicates objects to another pocket/region (useful for DR), but ELA PROPER EXIGE that the versioning is enabled in the original and destination bucks; moreover, by default the CRR would replicate the SOBRESCRITA also corrupted, not providing, by itself, the ability to reverse to an earlier version of the same object.

Incorrect. Life cycle policies only TRANSICIONAM objects between storage classes (or exhales them) based on age — they do not create or preserve previous versions of an overwritten or excluded object, not helping in the recovery of the described incident.

Incorrect. Periodic manual copies are operationally costly, prone to human error and would only capture the state of the pocket at the time of copying — changes made between one copy and another (such as the overwriting of the scenario) could be lost, unlike Versioning, which protects CADA change automatically.

saa-med-105.text: The main infrastructure of a company runs in the us-east region-1. As part of the disaster recovery plan, a standby environment was provided in the us-west region-2. The company wants that, if the main application (us-east-1) stop responding, traffic DNS of customers be redirected AUTOMATICAMENTE for the standby environment, with the minimum impact perceptible to users. Amazon Route 53 meets this requirement?
options: Use a single record CNAME pointing to us-east-1 and update it manually to us-west-2 if the primary environment is unavailable.
Configure records with Failover routing policy, associating a Health Check with the primary endpoint in us-east-1 and defining the us-west record-2 as a secondary.
Configure records with Latency-based policy, pointing to us-east-1 and us-west-2.
Configure records with Weighted Routing Policy, distributing 90% from traffic to us-east-1 and 10% for us-west-2.
saa-med-105.explanation: The policy of routing Failover of Route 53 monitors the health of the primary resource through a Health Check; while the primary is healthy, the DNS If Health Check detects failure, the Route 53 automatically resolves to secondary resource (standby in us-west)-2) — exactly the described automatic DR behavior, without manual intervention.
saa-med-105.hint: Think about what policy of routing the Route 53 uses health checks to automatically switch between a primary and a secondary resource.
optionRationales: The policy of routing Failover of Route 53 monitors the health of the primary resource through a Health Check; while the primary is healthy, the DNS If Health Check detects failure, the Route 53 automatically resolves to secondary resource (standby in us-west)-2) — exactly the described automatic DR behavior, without manual intervention.

Incorrect. Weighted routing distributes traffic based on PESOS FIXOS, regardless of the health of the endpoints — it was not designed to alternate to the standby environment SOMENTE when the primary fails, can send traffic to us-east-1 Even when she's out of the air.

Incorrect. This approach is manual (requires human intervention to detect failure and update the DNS) and suffers from the delay in propagation caused by the cache of DNS (TTL), significantly increasing the time of unavailability perceived by users.

Incorrect as the main solution for this scenario. Latency routing directs users to the region with MENOR Network LATENCIA from your location — your purpose is to optimize performance, not implement a primary/standard disaster recovery based on availability of the primary environment.

saa-med-106.text: A request processing application is executed in instances EC2 who, upon receiving an application, call SINCRONAMENTE a payment processing service. During peaks of traffic or temporary unavailabilities of the payment service, these calls fail and the corresponding requests are PERDIDOS. The company wants no request to be lost in these situations, allowing the processing to be automatically resumed when the payment service recovers. What architectural change solves this problem?
options: Insert a row Amazon SQS between the application of orders and the payment service: the application sends a message to the queue for each order, and a fleet of workers consumes the queue and calls the payment service, with the message remaining in the queue until it is successfully processed.
Increase the number of instances EC2 processing requests to handle more simultaneous calls to the payment service.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff directly in the application code EC2, without using a row.
Enable Multi-AZ in the instance of Amazon RDS which stores the applications.
saa-med-106.explanation: Correct. By decoupling the receipt of the payment processing request via Amazon SQS, each order is stored in a DURABLE manner in the queue. If the payment service is unavailable or overloaded, the messages simply stay in the queue (without being lost) until the workers succeed in processing them — meeting exactly the requirement not to lose orders and automatically resume.
saa-med-106.hint: Think about which service allows you to thread messages in a durable way between two components, absorbing peaks and temporary unavailabilities of the consumer.
optionRationales: Correct. By decoupling the receipt of the payment processing request via Amazon SQS, each order is stored in a DURABLE manner in the queue. If the payment service is unavailable or overloaded, the messages simply stay in the queue (without being lost) until the workers succeed in processing them — meeting exactly the requirement not to lose orders and automatically resume.

Incorrect. Adding more instances increases the CAPACIDADE of simultaneous calls, but does not solve the problem of PERDA OF PEDIDOS when the payment service is unavailable — more instances calling an out-of-the-air service still result in lost orders and failures.

Incorrect. RDS protects against the inavailability of the BANCO OF DADOS, but has no relation to the synchronous communication between the application of orders and the payment service, which is the cause of the loss of orders described.

Incorrect as a complete solution. Backoff Retries improve resilience to failures BREVES, but the state of the attempts remains APENAS IN THE MEMORY of the instance — if the instance EC2 reboot or be replaced during a prolonged non-availability of the payment service, requests in retry would be lost. (SQS) preserves requests regardless of the life cycle of the instances.

saa-med-107.text: One Auto Scaling Group is configured with the standard health check, based only on EC2. The team realized that when the PROCESSO APPLICATION within a locking instance (but the instance EC2 continues running and passes status checks on EC2), o ALB returns errors 502 for users, and Auto Scaling Group DOES NOT replace this instance. The team wants instances with the locked application to be detected and replaced automatically. What change solves this problem?
options: Change the type of health check Auto Scaling Group for ELB and set up a health check in the target group of ALB checking an endpoint of the application.
Create an alarm from CloudWatch based on the CPUtilization metric to trigger a scaling action.
Increase the cooldown period of the Auto Scaling Group.
Keep the type of health check standard (EC2), which already checks the status of the operating system and the instance hardware.
saa-med-107.explanation: Correct. By setting the health check type of ASG as ELB, o Auto Scaling Group is considering an instance as not complete if it FALHAR in the health check of the target group of ALB (testing the application, not just the status of EC2). Cases marked as unhealthy by ALB are automatically closed and replaced by ASG, solving the implementation scenario locked.
saa-med-107.hint: Think about what kind of health check Auto Scaling Group allows the result of the load balancer integrity check to determine whether an instance should be replaced.
optionRationales: Correct. By setting the health check type of ASG as ELB, o Auto Scaling Group is considering an instance as not complete if it FALHAR in the health check of the target group of ALB (testing the application, not just the status of EC2). Cases marked as unhealthy by ALB are automatically closed and replaced by ASG, solving the implementation scenario locked.

Incorrect. The cooldown controls the range between ACTIONS OF ESCALABILIDADE (to avoid overreactions to metrics), but does not affect how ASG determines whether an instance is complete — does not resolve the detection of an application blocked.

Incorrect. A blocked application may present use of CPU NORMAL or even low — monitor CPUtilization does not detect this type of application level failure, which is only perceived through (or missing) responses to requests HTTP, checked by the health check of ALB.

That's exactly the behavior. ATUAL of the scenario, which DOES NOT solve the problem — the status checks of the EC2 confirm that the hypervisor/operational system is working, but do not check if the APPLICATION within the instance is responding correctly.

saa-med-108.text: A three-layer application has instances EC2 of the application layer in subnets PRIVADAS, distributed in two Availability Zones (AZ-A and AZ-B). These instances need access to the internet (e.g. to download package updates), but should not be reachable from the internet. The team wants a network architecture in which the failure of the component of NAT in one AZ does not affect the output connectivity of the instances in the other AZ. Which design meets this requirement?
options: Provide a single NAT Gateway in AZ-A and configure the route tables of the private sub-networks of AZ-A and AZ-B to use this same NAT Gateway.
Attach one Internet Gateway directly to the route tables of the private sub-networks.
Replace NAT Gateways for a single instance EC2 configured as NAT instance, shared by both AZs.
Provide one NAT Gateway in the public sub-network of each AZ (one in AZ-A, other in AZ-B) and configure the route table of each private sub-network to use the NAT Gateway of MESMA AZ.
saa-med-108.explanation: Correct. NAT Gateway by AZ and route the outbound traffic of each private sub-network through the NAT Gateway of SUA AZ, each AZ becomes independent: if NAT Gateway of AZ-A present some problem, only the private sub-networks of AZ-A are affected, while AZ-B continues to operate normally — eliminating the single point of failure between AZs.
saa-med-108.hint: Think of having a component of NAT independent by Availability Zone, with each private sub-network routing to the NAT of SUA AZ PROPERLY.
optionRationales: Correct. NAT Gateway by AZ and route the outbound traffic of each private sub-network through the NAT Gateway of SUA AZ, each AZ becomes independent: if NAT Gateway of AZ-A present some problem, only the private sub-networks of AZ-A are affected, while AZ-B continues to operate normally — eliminating the single point of failure between AZs.

Incorrect. NAT Gateway be highly available DENTRO from his own AZ, he's still a resource ZONAL: if AZ-A be unavailable, private sub-networks of AZ-B (which depend on NAT Gateway in AZ-A) they would lose access to the internet — creating exactly the single point of failure between AZs that the requirement seeks to avoid (in addition to generating data transfer costs between AZs)).

Incorrect. NAT instance is a resource managed by the client (without high native availability), subject to the capacity limits of the instance itself and requiring manual failure configuration — in addition to, as a shared unique resource, still represent a single point of failure for both AZs.

Incorrect. Add a direct route to a Internet Gateway would effectively make these subnets PUBLIC (and would require public IPs in instances for communication to work), violating the requirement that application layer instances should not be accessible from the internet.
